sections.heading: The present perfect subjunctive
sections.body: Form: present subjunctive of *haber* + past participle.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body:
It's the subjunctive version of the present perfect (*he terminado*): a completed action, looked at from now, after a subjunctive trigger.

- *Espero que hayas llegado bien.* (I hope you got there OK.)
- *Me alegra que hayas venido.* (I'm glad you came.)
- *No creo que haya terminado.* (I don't think he's finished.)
- *Es posible que se hayan perdido.* (They may have gotten lost.)
- *Ojalá haya aprobado.* (I hope she passed.)
- With future time clauses, for something completed by then: *Llámame cuando hayas terminado.* (Call me when you've finished.)

Compare: *Espero que llegues bien* (I hope you arrive safely — future) vs. *Espero que hayas llegado bien* (I hope you arrived safely — already done).

Ojalá haya aprobado el examen.
I hope she passed the exam.
Llámame cuando hayas terminado.

Espero que llegues bien.
I hope you arrive safely.
Dudo que hayan recibido el paquete.
I doubt they've received the package.
Es raro que no haya llamado.
It's strange that he hasn't called.
Siento que hayas tenido un mal día.
I'm sorry you've had a bad day.
Me sorprende que no te hayas dado cuenta.
I'm surprised you haven't noticed.
No hay nadie que haya visto la película.
There's nobody who's seen the movie.
Espero que no se hayan olvidado de mí.
I hope they haven't forgotten me.
Cuando hayamos comido, salimos.
When we've eaten, we'll leave.
Ojalá hayan arreglado la computadora.
I hope they've fixed the computer.
No es verdad que lo haya dicho.
It's not true that she said it.
